request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.

agent.result_text:
I added the tree export button, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** pressing the button (`data-testid="export-tree"`) downloads `tree-<sheet>.csv`. The first line is `sheet,name,grade,due-total`. Then come this sheet's people in list order, then the people of the other sheets in the tree — its parents above it and its child sheets below — sorted by sheet id. Each person's grade is the one in force on their own sheet's today, and their due-total matches what their row shows on that sheet (`n/a` when there isn't one).

**How it's built:** it's one new frontend file, `src/main/frontend/features/export/exportTree.slot.tsx`, modelled on the existing tree search. It gets the other sheet ids from the existing `GET /api/sheets/{id}/tree` endpoint, then works out each sheet's lines with the same per-person due calculation the people list uses. It waits until every sheet's data has been freshly loaded before it downloads. Nothing changed on the server or in the database.

**Before reusing it:** the button is disabled while an export is being prepared.
